glosses: to frame (construct in words so as to establish a context for understanding or interpretation)

examples.text: In den USA gibt es nach der Veröffentlichung der Überwachungszahlen nun Versuche, die Geräte neu zu framen – also durch eine Umbenennung auf die weniger positiven Seiten hinzuweisen. Der Name beeinflusst schließlich die Einstellung zum Produkt.
examples.translation: In the US there are now, according to publications of the surveillance numbers, attempts to reframe the items – i.e. pointing out the less positive aspects by renaming it. The name influences the attitude towards the product after all.

examples.text: „In den USA gibt es nach der Veröffentlichung der Überwachungszahlen nun Versuche, die Geräte neu zu framen – also durch eine Umbenennung auf die weniger positiven Seiten hinzuweisen. Der Name beeinflusst schließlich die Einstellung zum Produkt.“
„Manipulanten framen zum Beispiel ihr Eingeständnis, gelogen zu haben, in Anlehnung an Nachbessern, neuerdings mit einem ‚Nachinformieren‘.“
„Andererseits dürfte die Chance auf Berücksichtigung umso höher sein, je mehr Akteure die Berichterstattung auf die gleiche Weise zu framen versuchen.“

„Insgesamt aber muss das außergewöhnliche Verhalten eines Akteurs als gesellschaftlich und moralisch legitimes Verhalten geframet werden, um möglichst eine breite positive oder neutrale Kolportierung in den Massenmedien zu erfahren.“

„Es lässt sich also annehmen, dass die Migration aus SSA überwiegend als »Bedrohung« und »Ansturm« geframt wird, was im folgenden Kapitel durch die Diskursanalyse der Zeitungsartikel zu untersuchen ist.“

„Gleichzeitig war zu sehen, dass die Begriffe Verantwortung und Solidarität zwar durchaus häufig verwendet wurden, doch der geringe Bezug zu solidarischem Handeln in Gestalt des Begriffes Hilfen fehlte und andererseits Verantwortung vor allem als Eigenverantwortung geframt wurde […]“

glosses: To fit, as for a specific end or purpose; make suitable or comfortable; adapt; adjust.

examples.text: I will hereafter frame myself to be coy.
frame my face to all occasions
We may in some measure frame our minds for the reception of happiness.
The human mind is framed to be influenced.

glosses: To construct by fitting together or uniting various parts; fabricate by union of constituent parts.

examples.text:
Nature that fram’d vs of foure Elements,
Warring within our breaſts for regiment,
Doth teach vs all to haue aſpyring minds:

glosses: To bring or put into form or order; adjust the parts or elements of; compose; contrive; plan; devise.

examples.text: He began to frame the loveliest countenance he could.
How many excellent reasonings are framed in the mind of a man of wisdom and study in a length of years.
As for America’s constitution, speaking as the court’s originalist-in-chief, all that mattered was what its words meant when it was framed.

glosses: Of a constructed object such as a building, to put together the structural elements.

examples.text: Once we finish framing the house, we'll hang tin on the roof.

glosses: Of a picture such as a painting or photograph, to place inside a decorative border.
To position visually within a fixed boundary.

examples.text: The director frames the fishing scene very well.

glosses: To construct in words so as to establish a context for understanding or interpretation.

examples.text: How would you frame your accomplishments?
The way the opposition has framed the argument makes it hard for us to win.

glosses: Conspire to falsely incriminate an innocent person.

examples.text: The gun had obviously been placed in her car in an effort to frame her.

examples.text: An oath, and a threat to set Throttler on me if I did not "frame off" rewarded my perseverance.

glosses: To proceed; to go.

examples.text: The beautie of this ſinfull Dame, / Made many Princes thither frame, / To ſeeke her as a bedfellow, / In maryage pleaſures, playfellow:

glosses: To hit (the ball) with the frame of the racquet rather than the strings (normally a mishit).

glosses: To cause; to bring about; to produce.

examples.text: Fear frames disorder, and disorder wounds.

examples.text: When thou hast turned them all ways, and done thy best to hew them and to make them frame, thou must be fain to cast them out.

glosses: To succeed in doing or trying to do something; manage.

examples.text: Now that the frame is complete, we can start on the walls.

glosses: Anything composed of parts fitted and united together; a fabric; a structure.

examples.text:

Enchac’d with thouſands euer ſhining lamps,
Will ſooner burne the glorious frame of Heauen,
Then ſhould it ſo conſpire my ouerthrow.

glosses: A human body or the structure thereof; the size, shape, sturdiness etc. of a person's body as described in a certain way; one's build.

examples.text: His starved flesh hung loosely on his once imposing frame.

glosses: A rigid, generally rectangular mounting for paper, canvas or other flexible material.

examples.text: He looked round the poor room, at the distempered walls, and the bad engravings in meretricious frames, the crinkly paper and wax flowers on the chiffonier; and he thought of a room like Father Bryan's, with panelling, with cut glass, with tulips in silver pots, such a room as he had hoped to have for his own.

examples.text: In knockemdowns and bowls ten pins are used, the centre one being called the king, and the ball has to be grounded before it reaches the frame.
